key_insight: An agentic, three-layer architecture leverages LLMs to translate natural-language research questions into validated, executable scientific workflows, closing the semantic gap between scientific intent and workflow execution.
problem_solved: Scientists must manually convert research questions into workflow specifications—requiring domain knowledge and infrastructure expertise—which creates friction, errors, and poor reproducibility in scientific automation.
method: Three-layer agentic design: (1) Semantic layer — LLMs parse natural language into structured intents; (2) Generator layer — validated generators synthesize reproducible workflow components/specs; (3) Execution layer — orchestrates generated workflows on scientific workflow systems with scheduling, fault tolerance, and resource management.
Validation and provenance: generators include checks, templates, and provenance metadata to ensure reproducibility and traceability of produced workflows.
Integration and human-in-the-loop: interfaces for expert review and iterative refinement, plus connectors to existing workflow engines and infrastructure for end-to-end automation.
impact: Reduces the technical barrier for turning research questions into reproducible experiments, accelerating experiment lifecycle and improving reliability for AI/ML practitioners and domain scientists.

paper_title: From Research Question to Scientific Workflow: Leveraging Agentic AI for Science Automation
